title: UNIT: METALS, NON-METALS AND THEIR EXTRACTION
notes:
✓ Metals → Generally lustrous, malleable, ductile and good conductors of heat and electricity.

✓ Non-metals → Generally poor conductors and may be brittle in the solid state.

title: 1. Metals and Non-metals
notes:
✓ Metals → Usually lose electrons to form positive ions and have metallic bonding.

They are generally hard, strong, malleable, ductile and good conductors.

✓ Non-metals → Usually gain or share electrons. They are generally dull, brittle when solid and poor conductors, with graphite as an important exception.

◆ EXAMPLES
✓ Metals → Al, Fe, Cu, Na.
✓ Non-metals → N, O, S, Cl, P.

title: 2. Mineral, Ore and Metallurgy
notes:
✓ Mineral → A naturally occurring substance containing a metal or its compounds.

✓ Ore → A mineral from which a metal can be extracted economically.

✓ Metallurgy → The science and processes involved in extracting metals from their ores and refining them.

◆ MAIN STEPS
✓ Concentration of ore.
✓ Conversion to oxide or suitable compound.
✓ Reduction to metal.
✓ Refining.

title: 3. Roasting and Calcination
notes:
✓ Roasting → Heating a concentrated ore strongly in excess air, usually to convert sulfide ores into oxides.

◆ EXAMPLE
2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂

✓ Calcination → Heating an ore strongly in limited or no air to remove volatile substances, commonly CO₂ or H₂O.

◆ EXAMPLE
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.

title: 4. Chemical Reduction
notes:
✓ Chemical reduction → The removal of oxygen from a metal compound using a reducing agent such as carbon, carbon monoxide or hydrogen.

◆ EXAMPLE
Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂

→ It is suitable for metals that are less reactive than the reducing agent.

title: 5. Electrolytic Reduction
notes:
✓ Electrolytic reduction → Uses electricity to reduce metal ions to metals.

→ It is used for highly reactive metals that cannot be obtained easily by chemical reduction.

◆ EXAMPLES
✓ Aluminium → Electrolytic reduction of alumina.
✓ Sodium, magnesium and calcium → Electrolysis of molten salts.

title: 6. Aluminium: Occurrence and Extraction
notes:
✓ Aluminium → Mainly obtained from bauxite, an important aluminium ore.

→ Alumina (Al₂O₃) is purified from bauxite and then electrolytically reduced.

◆ HALL PROCESS
✓ Purified Al₂O₃ is dissolved in molten cryolite.
✓ Cryolite lowers the melting point and improves electrical conductivity.
✓ Electrolysis produces aluminium at the cathode.

◆ CATHODE
Al³⁺ + 3e⁻ → Al

✓ Aluminium is widely used because it is light, corrosion-resistant and a good conductor.

title: 7. Cryolite
notes:
✓ Cryolite → Na₃AlF₆ and is used in the electrolytic extraction of aluminium.

◆ FUNCTIONS
✓ Lowers the melting point of alumina.
✓ Increases electrical conductivity.
✓ Helps keep the electrolyte molten during electrolysis.

title: 8. Iron: Occurrence and Extraction
notes:
◆ IMPORTANT IRON ORES
✓ Hematite → Fe₂O₃.
✓ Magnetite → Fe₃O₄.
✓ Limonite.
✓ Siderite → FeCO₃.

✓ Iron → Mainly extracted in a blast furnace.

→ Concentrated ore is reduced by carbon monoxide produced from coke.

◆ MAIN REACTION
Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂

✓ Limestone → Removes impurities by forming slag.

title: 9. Blast Furnace
notes:
✓ Blast furnace → Used for extracting iron from iron ore.

◆ RAW MATERIALS
✓ Iron ore.
✓ Coke.
✓ Limestone.
✓ Hot air.

✓ Coke → Produces heat and CO, which reduces iron oxide.
✓ Limestone → Decomposes to CaO, which reacts with silica impurity to form slag.

CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂
CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃ (slag).

title: 10. Slag
notes:
✓ Slag → A molten waste material formed when impurities in an ore react with a flux during extraction.

◆ IRON EXTRACTION
CaO + SiO₂ → CaSiO₃

→ The calcium silicate slag is separated from molten iron because it is less dense.

title: 11. Steel and Alloy
notes:
✓ Steel → An alloy mainly consisting of iron and carbon, often with other elements.

✓ Alloy → A mixture of two or more elements in which at least one is a metal.

→ Alloys are produced to improve properties such as strength, hardness, corrosion resistance and durability.

◆ EXAMPLES
✓ Steel → Fe + C.
✓ Stainless steel → Fe with Cr and other elements.
✓ Brass → Cu + Zn.

title: 12. Bessemer Converter
notes:
✓ Bessemer converter → Used to convert molten pig iron into steel by blowing air through it.

→ Impurities such as carbon, silicon and manganese are oxidized.

→ The heat produced by oxidation keeps the molten metal hot.

✓ The process produces steel rapidly but has largely been replaced by modern steelmaking methods.

title: 13. Basic Oxygen Process
notes:
✓ Basic oxygen process → A modern method of steel production in which pure oxygen is blown into molten pig iron.

→ Oxygen oxidizes excess carbon and other impurities.
→ A basic flux helps remove acidic impurities as slag.

◆ ADVANTAGES
✓ Fast steel production.
✓ Good control of composition.
✓ Suitable for large-scale production.

title: 14. Open-Hearth Furnace
notes:
✓ Open-hearth furnace → An older method of producing steel by heating pig iron and scrap steel while controlling the oxidation of impurities.

→ It allows careful control of carbon content and steel composition but is slower and less efficient than modern oxygen steelmaking.

title: 15. Thermite Process
notes:
✓ Thermite process → Uses aluminium powder to reduce certain metal oxides and produce molten metal.

◆ EXAMPLE
Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → 2Fe + Al₂O₃ + heat

→ The reaction produces a very large amount of heat and is used for welding railway tracks and obtaining some metals.

title: 16. Blister Copper
notes:
✓ Blister copper → Impure copper obtained during the extraction of copper from sulfide ores. It contains about 98–99% copper.

→ It is called blister copper because escaping gases during solidification leave a blistered surface.

✓ It is further purified by electrolytic refining.

title: 17. Nitrogen: Occurrence and Properties
notes:
✓ Nitrogen (N₂) → A colorless, odorless gas that makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

→ It is relatively unreactive because N₂ has a strong triple bond.

◆ USES
✓ Manufacture of ammonia.
✓ Production of fertilizers.
✓ Inert atmosphere for food and industrial processes.

title: 18. Haber Process
notes:
✓ Haber process → Produces ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen.

N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃

◆ CONDITIONS
✓ High pressure.
✓ Moderate temperature.
✓ Iron catalyst.

→ Ammonia is mainly used to manufacture fertilizers and other nitrogen compounds.

title: 19. Phosphorus: Occurrence and Properties
notes:
✓ Phosphorus → Does not occur freely in nature because it is reactive.

→ It occurs mainly as phosphate minerals such as rock phosphate and fluoroapatite.

◆ IMPORTANT ALLOTROPES
✓ White phosphorus → Very reactive, poisonous and stored under water.
✓ Red phosphorus → Less reactive, more stable and used on safety-match surfaces.

title: 20. Rock Phosphate and Fluoroapatite
notes:
✓ Rock phosphate → A natural source of phosphate minerals and an important raw material for phosphorus compounds and fertilizers.

✓ Fluoroapatite → A phosphate mineral with approximate formula Ca₅(PO₄)₃F. It is an important natural source of phosphorus.

title: 21. Red Phosphorus
notes:
✓ Red phosphorus → An allotrope of phosphorus.

◆ PROPERTIES
✓ More stable than white phosphorus.
✓ Less reactive.
✓ Not as poisonous as white phosphorus.
✓ Does not glow in air under ordinary conditions.

✓ Use → Safety matches and some flame-retardant materials.

title: 22. White Phosphorus
notes:
✓ White phosphorus → A highly reactive allotrope of phosphorus.

◆ PROPERTIES
✓ Waxy solid.
✓ Poisonous.
✓ Glows in air.
✓ Ignites easily.
✓ Stored under water to prevent contact with oxygen.

→ It is more reactive and less stable than red phosphorus.

title: 23. Oxygen: Occurrence and Properties
notes:
✓ Oxygen (O₂) → A colorless, odorless gas that supports combustion but is not itself a fuel.

→ It occurs in the atmosphere, water, minerals and many oxides.

◆ USES
✓ Respiration.
✓ Medical oxygen.
✓ Welding and cutting.
✓ Steel production.

title: 24. Sulphur: Occurrence and Properties
notes:
✓ Sulphur → A yellow non-metal that occurs both in the free state and in compounds such as sulfide and sulfate minerals.

◆ PROPERTIES
✓ Yellow solid.
✓ Poor conductor of electricity.
✓ Burns in oxygen with a blue flame.

S + O₂ → SO₂

◆ USES
✓ Manufacture of sulfuric acid.
✓ Fertilizers.
✓ Rubber products.
✓ Chemicals.

title: 25. Frasch Process
notes:
✓ Frasch process → Used to extract underground elemental sulfur.

→ Superheated water is forced underground to melt sulfur.
→ Compressed air then pushes the molten sulfur to the surface through pipes.

✓ It is suitable for sulfur deposits located underground.

title: 26. Contact Process
notes:
✓ Contact process → Used to manufacture sulfuric acid.

◆ MAIN STEPS
✓ Sulfur is burned to form SO₂.
✓ SO₂ is oxidized to SO₃.
✓ SO₃ is absorbed to form sulfuric acid.

◆ KEY REACTION
2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃

◆ CONDITIONS
✓ V₂O₅ catalyst.
✓ About 450°C.
✓ Suitable pressure.

title: 27. Chlorine: Occurrence and Properties
notes:
✓ Chlorine (Cl₂) → A greenish-yellow, toxic gas with a characteristic smell.

→ It occurs mainly as chloride ions in salts such as sodium chloride because it is highly reactive.

◆ USES
✓ Water disinfection.
✓ Manufacture of PVC and other chemicals.
✓ Bleaching.
✓ Production of hydrochloric acid and chlorinated compounds.

title: 28. Fractional Distillation
notes:
✓ Fractional distillation → Separates a mixture of liquids based on differences in their boiling points.

→ It is used to separate liquid air into nitrogen, oxygen and other gases after cooling air to a liquid state.

✓ Nitrogen has a lower boiling point than oxygen, so it is separated first.

title: 29. Allotrope
notes:
✓ Allotrope → One of two or more different structural forms of the same element in the same physical state.

◆ EXAMPLES
✓ Carbon → Diamond, graphite.
✓ Phosphorus → White phosphorus, red phosphorus.
✓ Oxygen → O₂ and O₃.

title: 30. MUST REMEMBER
notes:
◆ METALLURGY
✓ Metallurgy → Extraction and purification of metals.
✓ Ore → Mineral from which metal is economically extracted.

◆ METAL EXTRACTION
✓ Bauxite → Major ore of aluminium.
✓ Cryolite → Lowers melting point of alumina and improves conductivity.
✓ Blast furnace → Extraction of iron.
✓ Bessemer converter → Older steelmaking process.
✓ Basic oxygen process → Modern steelmaking process.
✓ Thermite process → Aluminium reduces metal oxide.

◆ NITROGEN
✓ Nitrogen → About 78% of air.
✓ Haber process → NH₃ production.

◆ PHOSPHORUS
✓ Phosphorus → Rock phosphate and fluoroapatite.
✓ White phosphorus → Highly reactive.
✓ Red phosphorus → More stable.

◆ SULPHUR
✓ Sulphur → Frasch process.
✓ Sulfuric acid → Contact process.

◆ CHLORINE AND AIR
✓ Chlorine → Greenish-yellow reactive gas.
✓ Liquid air → Fractional distillation gives N₂ and O₂.

◆ EXAM TIP
✓ Remember the extraction keywords:
Aluminium → Electrolytic reduction.
Iron → Blast furnace.
Sulfur → Frasch process.
Ammonia → Haber process.
Sulfuric acid → Contact process.
Air → Fractional distillation.
